title: Hof restore evidence
description: Written atomically once a restore operation reaches its own end (ADR 0006's own Restore Flow step 12) - immutable once written. Kept entirely separate from the restored installation's own generation history (state-v1.schema.json has no restore-provenance field at all, by design - a restored installationId/generation must read exactly as if that generation had always lived on this hardware, with the fact that it arrived via a restore recorded only here, never folded into current.json itself).

planId.description: The restore-plan-v1 planId this evidence resulted from.

snapshotId.description: The exact restic snapshot id actually restored from - restore-plan-v1 itself only names backupId+destinationName; this is the concrete snapshot snapshot.verify resolved and pinned before any data.restore ran.

manifestDigest.description: sha256 of the backup-manifest-v1 document embedded in the restored snapshot, verified before trusting anything else in it.

recoveryKitDigest.description: sha256 of the recovery-kit-v1 document actually used - must equal both restore-plan-v1's own recoveryKitDigest and the manifest's own recoveryKitDigest, confirmed before secret.materialize ever ran.

backupToolLockDigest.description: The signed backup-tool-lock this restore actually ran under.

source.description: The historical installation this restore recovered - see restore-plan-v1's own identical shape.

target.description: The new host this was actually restored onto.

dataRestoredCheckpointAt.description: When checkpoint.data-restored was durably recorded - null if the operation never reached it (a --resume before this point may still delete this operation's own volumes and restart materialization from nothing; a --resume after it never rewrites data again).

readinessConfirmedAt.description: When readiness.wait last confirmed the fully-restored platform ready - null unless status is succeeded. Never non-null on a failed restore: readiness.wait is the step immediately before evidence.write, so a restore that reached and confirmed readiness has nothing left that could still fail the overall operation.

abandoned.description: true only when this terminal failed evidence was written because the operator explicitly gave up on a stuck, still-in-progress operationId (restore has no guaranteed finally block the way backup does - a restore that gets stuck before reaching its own natural evidence.write has no other path to a terminal state). false for every other outcome, succeeded or a real in-flow failure that itself reached evidence.write. Always false when status: succeeded.

error.description: Only for status: failed - a short, sanitized diagnostic. Never a raw exception dump, a secret value, decrypted content, or an SSH private-key path.
